stories.headline: Apple commits over $30B to Broadcom for 15 billion US-made chips, its biggest manufacturing pledge

key_facts.fact: Apple announced on July 8, 2026 a new multiyear commitment with Broadcom, expected to exceed $30 billion, that will lead to production of more than 15 billion U.S.-made chips and support hundreds of American jobs.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple today announced a new multiyear commitment with Broadcom to design and produce custom silicon components and cutting-edge wireless connectivity technologies for a wide range of Apple products. The new agreement, expected to exceed $30 billion, will lead to the production of more than 15 billion U.S.-made chips and support hundreds of American jobs.

key_facts.fact: It is Apple's largest commitment to date under its American Manufacturing Program (AMP), launched last year, and will let Broadcom expand and modernize its Fort Collins, Colorado plant with $1.5 billion of capital expenditure.
key_facts.excerpt: This new agreement, which marks Apple's largest AMP commitment to date, will enable Broadcom to expand and modernize its manufacturing facilities in Fort Collins, Colorado, with a $1.5 billion capital expenditure investment.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom will produce advanced radio frequency components — including FBAR filters — and advanced wireless connectivity technologies at the Fort Collins facility.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom will produce advanced radio frequency components — including FBAR filters — and advanced wireless connectivity technologies at the Fort Collins facility.

key_facts.fact: The spending is part of Apple's pledge to invest $600 billion in the U.S. economy over four years, and Apple explicitly thanked the Trump administration for backing the project.
key_facts.excerpt: These investments are part of Apple's commitment to invest $600 billion in the U.S. economy over four years... 'We're grateful to the president and his administration for supporting important projects like this one.'

key_facts.fact: Tim Cook framed the deal as part of building an end-to-end silicon supply chain in America: 'Apple and Broadcom have a long history together, and this new phase of our partnership further accelerates our commitment to American manufacturing and innovation.'
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has been working with the administration and businesses across the U.S. to help create an end-to-end silicon supply chain in America, and today's announcement advances those efforts.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said the company is 'pleased to expand our manufacturing footprint in Fort Collins.'
key_facts.excerpt: "Broadcom is proud to continue to work with Apple after decades of success together, and we share a strong commitment to American innovation," said Hock Tan, Broadcom's president and CEO.

key_facts.fact: The expanded deal calls for 15 billion U.S.-made chips, according to Axios.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple's expanded Broadcom deal calls for 15 billion U.S.-made chips

Apple's expanded Broadcom deal calls for 15 billion U.S.-made chips

stories.headline: AI chip startup SambaNova raises $1B at $11B valuation, lands JPMorganChase as inference customer

key_facts.fact: SambaNova announced on July 8, 2026 the first close of $1 billion in strategic Series F financing, valuing the company at $11 billion post-money, led by General Atlantic.
key_facts.excerpt: SambaNova today announced it has completed the first close of $1 billion in strategic financing as part of a Series F round, valuing the company at $11 billion post money. This latest financing round was led by General Atlantic.

key_facts.fact: Seligman Ventures, T. Rowe Price Associates and Capital Group made significant investments; other new and existing investors include Battery Ventures, BlackRock-managed funds, Intel Capital, Qatar Investment Authority and Vista Equity Partners.
key_facts.excerpt: with significant investment from Seligman Ventures, T. Rowe Price Associates, Inc., and Capital Group. New and existing investors include A&E Investment, Assam Ventures, Battery Ventures, funds and accounts managed by BlackRock, Cambium Capital, Intel Capital, Kabila Capital, QFO Capital, Qatar Investment Authority (QIA), Vista Equity Partners and Volantis.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the raise, SambaNova said JPMorganChase selected it as an inference infrastructure partner, deploying its SN40 and SN50 systems to run secure, on-premises AI inference inside the bank.
key_facts.excerpt: SambaNova also announced that JPMorganChase has selected the company as an inference infrastructure partner, deploying its SN40 and SN50 systems to power secure, on-prem AI inference for the firm.

key_facts.fact: Darrin Alves, CIO of Infrastructure Platforms at JPMorganChase: 'AI infrastructure has to meet a very high bar for performance, control and reliability. We're excited to deploy SambaNova's RDU architecture.'
key_facts.excerpt: "At JPMorganChase, AI infrastructure has to meet a very high bar for performance, control and reliability," said Darrin Alves, CIO, Infrastructure Platforms, JPMorganChase.

key_facts.fact: The $11B valuation comes roughly five months after a $350 million Series E, and after Bloomberg reported in December that Intel had discussed acquiring SambaNova for about $1.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: AI chip maker SambaNova has raised at an $11B valuation months after Intel was rumored to be trying to buy it for about $1.6 billion.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2017 and based in San Jose, SambaNova sells chips, systems and cloud services built on its Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU) architecture, targeting enterprises, neoclouds, AI labs and sovereign AI projects.
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Jose, California, SambaNova delivers chips, systems, and cloud services that enable customers to deploy state-of-the-art models with superior performance, lower total cost of ownership, and rapid time to value.

key_facts.fact: CNBC framed the round as part of a wave of AI chip startups trying to challenge Nvidia's dominance.
key_facts.excerpt: SambaNova is valued at $11 billion after fresh financing led by General Atlantic, as AI chip startups look to challenge Nvidia.

stories.headline: Nvidia pairs its GPUs with rival d-Matrix's chips as Parasail deploys a mixed inference cluster

key_facts.fact: On July 8, 2026, inference cloud Parasail and chip startup d-Matrix announced Parasail is deploying d-Matrix Corsair inference accelerators alongside Nvidia Hopper and Blackwell GPUs, targeting up to 10x faster and more cost-efficient inference.
key_facts.excerpt: Parasail, the inference cloud for AI-native startups, and d-Matrix... today announced Parasail is deploying d-Matrix Corsair inference accelerators alongside the NVIDIA Hopper and NVIDIA Blackwell architectures to deliver up to 10x faster, more cost-efficient inference services to its customers.

key_facts.fact: The companies call it one of the first commercial-scale examples of 'heterogeneous disaggregated inference' in production: Nvidia GPUs handle compute-intensive prefill while Corsair handles latency-sensitive decode.
key_facts.excerpt: Parasail's Corsair deployment marks one of the first commercial-scale examples of heterogeneous disaggregated inference in production... combining NVIDIA GPUs for compute-intensive prefill with d-Matrix Corsair accelerators for latency-sensitive decode.

key_facts.fact: Corsair is built on TSMC's N6 process with organic substrates and LP-DDR5 memory, using a Digital In-Memory Compute chiplet architecture that d-Matrix says delivers up to 10x faster interactive inference and up to 3x better energy efficiency.
key_facts.excerpt: Corsair eliminates that penalty entirely, enabling up to 10x faster interactive inference and up to 3x better energy efficiency versus traditional approaches. Built on TSMC's N6 process with organic substrates and LP-DDR5 memory...

key_facts.fact: d-Matrix CEO Sid Sheth: 'GPUs and purpose-built inference accelerators aren't competitors; they're better together.' Parasail CEO Mike Henry said pairing Corsair with existing Hopper and Blackwell fleets extends the life of already-deployed hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: "Parasail is proving what we've believed from the start: the future of inference is heterogeneous," said Sid Sheth, founder and CEO of d-Matrix. "GPUs and purpose-built inference accelerators aren't competitors; they're better together."

key_facts.fact: Parasail aggregates GPU supply across more than 40 data centers in 15 countries; the companies plan to publish performance results after the first deployments and to explore expanding across that fleet.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies plan to share detailed performance results and case studies following the first series of deployments and explore expanded integration across Parasail's global fleet of over 40 data centers in 15 countries.

key_facts.fact: The Information reported that Nvidia and d-Matrix are combining their hardware in a new system to power AI models, describing it as Nvidia's strategy of partnering with its own chip competitors as a hedge.
key_facts.excerpt: In the latest example, Nvidia and AI chip startup d-Matrix are combining their respective hardware in a new system to power AI models

sources.title: Parasail to Combine NVIDIA AI Infrastructure with d-Matrix Accelerators to Achieve 10x Faster Token Generation

stories.headline: Apple begins testing DRAM from blacklisted Chinese memory maker CXMT for phones sold in China

key_facts.fact: Apple has begun testing DRAM chips from Chinese state-backed ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) for devices sold in China, according to two people familiar with the matter cited by the Financial Times.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has begun testing the company's DRam chips for devices sold in China, according to two people familiar with the matter, as the iPhone maker leads a lobbying effort among US tech companies to get the US government to allow broader use of the company's products.

key_facts.fact: Apple is leading a lobbying effort among US tech companies to get Washington to allow broader use of CXMT's products; Apple declined to comment on whether it was testing the chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple declined to comment on whether it was testing CXMT's chips for devices sold in China.

key_facts.fact: CXMT sits on a Pentagon blacklist over alleged military affiliations, and Apple has sought assurances that sourcing from it would not trigger further restrictions such as an Entity List designation.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT currently sits on a Pentagon blacklist due to concerns about military affiliations, which means Apple needs US government approval before any deals go through... Apple has been lobbying the US government for assurances that sourcing from CXMT won't trigger further restrictions, such as placement on the Entity List.

key_facts.fact: CXMT produces DDR5 and LPDDR5X chips that reportedly meet Apple's technical requirements for iPhones and other devices sold in the Chinese market.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT produces DDR5 and LPDDR5X chips that reportedly meet Apple's technical requirements for iPhones and other Apple devices, at least for the Chinese market.

key_facts.fact: CXMT has grown into the world's fourth-largest DRAM wafer producer, holding roughly 11% of capacity last year with projections to reach 15% by 2028, and is preparing a domestic IPO to fund capacity, next-generation DRAM and HBM work. Apple has not committed to commercial use.
key_facts.excerpt: CXMT has grown to become the fourth-largest global DRAM wafer producer, held roughly 11% of capacity last year with projections to reach 15% by 2028, and is planning a domestic IPO... Apple is testing CXMT-made DRAM for China-market devices and is engaging with U.S. regulators to broaden permitted use of the supplier's chips, without yet committing to commercial adoption.

key_facts.fact: Apple faced public pushback the last time it explored Chinese memory suppliers, including from then-senator Marco Rubio, who flagged security risks in 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple has previously faced public pushback from US policymakers when it last explored using Chinese memory suppliers, including then Republican senator Marco Rubio, who flagged security risks in 2022.

stories.headline: Quantum hardware startup Oratomic raises a $300M Series A to build a fault-tolerant machine

key_facts.fact: Oratomic announced on July 7, 2026 a $300 million Series A, co-led by ARCH Venture Partners, Spark Capital and Khosla Ventures.
key_facts.excerpt: We have raised a $300 million Series A, co-led by ARCH Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Khosla Ventures, alongside Bezos Expeditions, Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Lowercarbon Capital, Bain Capital, Formation, Nebular, David and Scott Aaronson, and others.

key_facts.fact: Additional backers include Bezos Expeditions, Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Lowercarbon Capital, Bain Capital, Formation, Nebular, and computer scientists David and Scott Aaronson.
key_facts.excerpt: Oratomic has secured $300 million in Series A funding, co-led by ARCH Venture Partners, Spark Capital, Bezos Expeditions, Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Lowercarbon Capital, Bain Capital, Formation, Nebular, David and Scott Aaronson, and others.

key_facts.fact: The money funds a single goal — the world's first fault-tolerant, utility-scale quantum computer — using reconfigurable atomic arrays trapped in focused laser beams. The company says it is not pursuing intermediate commercial products along the way.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is taking a different approach to quantum error correction, utilizing "reconfigurable atomic arrays trapped in focused laser beams"... as the company states, "We are not pursuing intermediate products or commercial systems along the way."

key_facts.fact: Oratomic launched in March 2026 out of research with Caltech scientists showing that a utility-scale fault-tolerant quantum computer could be built with 10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits, versus previous estimates of millions.
key_facts.excerpt: The new research demonstrates that utility-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers can be built with 10,000 reconfigurable atomic qubits, dramatically lowering the hardware threshold required for cryptographically relevant quantum computation, relative to previous estimates of millions of qubits.

key_facts.fact: Co-founder Manuel Endres has already trapped arrays of 6,000 atomic qubits; the founding team came from Caltech, Berkeley, Harvard, Amazon and Google.
key_facts.excerpt: neutral atoms are enabling faster scaling to large qubit numbers than any other quantum computing platform—Oratomic co-founder Manuel Endres has already trapped arrays of 6,000 atomic qubits.

key_facts.fact: The round is aimed at accelerating development of fault-tolerant, utility-scale quantum computers.
key_facts.excerpt: Oratomic raised a $300 million Series A to accelerate development of fault-tolerant, utility-scale quantum computers.

sources.title: $300M Series A Fuels Oratomic's Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computer Build
Oratomic Raises $300M in Series A Funding
Oratomic launches to build utility-scale quantum computers following breakthrough research

stories.headline: Omdia: sub-$400 phone shipments to fall 22% in 2026 as memory eats 60% of bill of materials

key_facts.fact: Omdia said on July 7, 2026 that sharply rising DRAM and NAND prices are driving a year-on-year decline of more than 22% in the global market for smartphones priced below $400.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Omdia's latest research, both DRAM and NAND prices have increased sharply over recent quarters and are expected to continue rising. Memory costs have become a serious burden for mid-to-low-end smartphones, contributing to a year-on-year decline of over 22% in the market for smartphones priced below $400.

key_facts.fact: In the first quarter of 2026, memory already accounted for nearly 60% of the total bill-of-materials cost in smartphones priced below $400, and more than 64% in phones under $99.
key_facts.excerpt: In 1Q26, memory costs already accounted for nearly 60% of the total BOM cost in smartphones priced below $400, and even exceeded 64% in products priced below $99.

key_facts.fact: Compared with the 3Q25-1Q26 cost structure, the memory share of BOM nearly doubled in the sub-$400 segment and rose more than 100% in phones above $400.
key_facts.excerpt: Compared with the BOM cost structure between 3Q25 and 1Q26, the memory cost share in 1Q26 nearly doubled in the sub-$400 price segment and increased by more than 100% in products priced above $400.

key_facts.fact: Vendors including Transsion, OPPO, vivo, Honor and Xiaomi have significantly raised retail prices just to hold thin margins, and are 'proactively and gradually retreating from the low-end segment' this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Smartphone vendors such as Transsion, OPPO, vivo, Honor and Xiaomi significantly raise the retail price of their products only to maintain thin profit margin... As a result, smartphone vendors are proactively and gradually retreating from the low-end segment in this year.

key_facts.fact: Omdia's May forecast has the global smartphone market shrinking 12% year-over-year in 2026, while shipments above $400 grow 5.7% — a widening split between cheap and premium phones.
key_facts.excerpt: According to Omdia's latest forecast in May, global smartphone market will decline by 12% year-over-year in 2026... By contrast, smartphone shipments above $400 will remain resilient and are expected to grow by 5.7% in 2026.

key_facts.fact: To offset memory costs in premium models, Chinese vendors are reverting from LTPO to LTPS OLED panels (saving $3-$5 per device) and slowing SoC upgrades by reusing previous-generation platforms, cutting SoC cost 30-40%.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese smartphone vendors are returning to LTPS OLED panel in some high-end models that had previously upgraded to LTPO display... This can save around $3 to $5 per device... vendors can slow down the pace of upgrades by using previous-generation platforms, potentially reducing costs by around 30% to 40%.

sources.title: Global smartphones priced below $400 will decline by 22% as memory costs soar
